outcome: complete blood count (CBC) variations (RDW, WBC, MCV, lymphocyte percentage)
cohort: The study included 137 neonates with clinical signs of sepsis (proven and suspected) and 50 healthy neonates as a control group.
finding: The study identified significant differences in various blood markers (elevated WBC, MCV, RDW, urea, D-dimer, ferritin, IL-10, hyperkalemia, reduced lymphocyte percentage) between septic and healthy neonates, suggesting their utility in predicting and monitoring neonatal sepsis.
mod_finding: The study reported that 76.12% of the neonates in the sepsis group were born via cesarean section.
